html:
November 5, 2026

Democrats sweep Congress in historic midterm landslide

tags: politics, elections
sources: @groundnews, @aaronparnas, @oafnation_actual

Democrats retook both chambers of Congress, flipping Republican Senate seats in Texas, South Carolina, Kansas, Iowa, Ohio, Maine and North Carolina and winning the national House popular vote by roughly 13 points, their largest margin since 1974. They are on track for about 250 to 260 House seats, enough that only around 30 Republicans would be needed to override a veto. Turnout was the second-highest for a midterm in over a century, about 94% of counties shifted left, and every age group under 65 and every major racial group moved toward Democrats. In North Carolina a Republican redistricting plan designed for an 11-3 advantage backfired, with Democrats leading in 10 of 14 districts, and Democrats also picked up five state-government trifectas.

Democrats plan sweeping investigations of Trump, Musk and corporate America

tags: politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas, @oafnation_actual

Incoming House Oversight Committee chair Robert Garcia said no one named Trump is off limits and that he wants Elon Musk, ICE officials and corporate executives testifying under oath, along with public hearings on the Epstein files. Democrats are also preparing investigations across banking, insurance, healthcare, media, energy and manufacturing, with companies that funded the White House ballroom described as early targets. Rep. Steve Scalise circulated a letter telling Republican colleagues to take inventory of likely oversight targets and prepare lists of programs, officials and outside allies. Administration officials are reported to be struggling to retain counsel, with few firms able to take on conflicting clients.

Hegseth faces bipartisan impeachment vote over Iran war

tags: politics, defence
sources: @aaronparnas, @oafnation_actual, @total.hypocrisy

Rep. Thomas Massie is set to call up articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth as soon as next week, with Republicans expected to join Democrats in supporting it. Hegseth released a video vowing not to back down and defending the Iran campaign, calling the impeachment push a sham, while Trump said he has done a fantastic job. Trump has been asking advisers whether Hegseth should remain in the job. Hegseth is not a candidate for Marsha Blackburn's open Tennessee Senate seat, which Blackburn will fill herself after being elected governor.

Senior Justice Department officials resign after midterm losses

tags: legal, politics
sources: @aaronparnas, @oafnation_actual

Three senior Justice Department officials resigned in two days: civil rights chief Harmeet Dhillon, US Attorney for the Southern District of Florida Jason Reding Quinones, whose office oversaw the election conspiracy probe of Trump's opponents, and national security division head John Eisenberg. Dhillon had overhauled the Civil Rights Division toward conservative causes since April 2025. Members of Congress have noted that departing officials can still be subpoenaed to testify. Further resignations are expected before the end of the year.

Stephen Miller named White House chief of staff as Susie Wiles departs

tags: politics
sources: @aaronparnas

Trump announced that Susie Wiles is leaving the administration and that Stephen Miller will take over as White House chief of staff beginning Monday. The change places the architect of the administration's immigration agenda in charge of White House operations. It follows the party's midterm defeat and a wider shakeup in Washington.

Vance and Rubio break with Trump over the Iran war

tags: politics, war
sources: @aaronparnas, @groundnews

Vice President JD Vance posted a message breaking with Trump on foreign policy and attributing the midterm losses to the war in Iran, reportedly sending it without White House clearance after a meeting intended to align post-election messaging. Vance's own account of the defeat cited polling in which voters said they wanted the war ended, a focus on cost of living, an America First posture and a changed relationship with Israel. Secretary of State Marco Rubio is expected to step down and launch a presidential campaign, possibly before the end of the year, seeking distance from the Iran campaign he helped direct.

Trump disputes results and turns to legacy projects as allies break away

tags: politics
sources: @aaronparnas, @oafnation_actual, @ericmoutsos

Trump said he was not on the ballot and would have won in a landslide if he had been, called US elections crooked and demanded that Alaska votes be awarded to Sen. Dan Sullivan, where Democrat Mary Peltola leads 48.2% to 47.9%. He cancelled public events after the losses, and reporting says he has largely disengaged from domestic issues to focus on foreign policy. Republicans including Marjorie Taylor Greene have publicly broken with him, and Ron DeSantis called the result close to an extinction-level event for the party. Trump signed an executive order designating the Oval Office and Cabinet Room a national landmark, while Judge Tanya Chutkan paused construction of his planned Washington arch for at least two weeks.

Markets sell off as investors price in limits on AI data centers

tags: markets, tech
sources: @groundnews, @oafnation_actual

US equities fell sharply as investors anticipated that Democratic control of Congress would bring restrictions on building the computing facilities that support artificial intelligence. The Dow lost 1,833 points, or 3.4%, the Nasdaq slid 5.5% into correction territory after falling more than 10% from its October peak, and the S&P 500 dropped 4.4%. Nvidia fell 9.2% and Advanced Micro Devices 17.3%. The administration also postponed a White House technology panel meeting that was to include Nvidia's Jensen Huang and Meta's Mark Zuckerberg.

Senate Democrats to probe JPMorgan's handling of Epstein accounts

tags: legal, politics
sources: @groundnews

Senate Finance Committee staff plan to investigate JPMorgan Chase's banking relationship with Jeffrey Epstein once Democrats take control of the chamber in January, including decisions by asset and wealth management head Mary Callahan Erdoes. Sen. Ron Wyden, the expected chair, has pledged to use the committee's subpoena power. A lawyer for the US Virgin Islands alleged in 2023 that the bank waited until after Epstein's death to report more than $1 billion in suspicious transactions, and Erdoes testified she knew of allegations involving underage girls in 2006 while the bank kept him as a client until 2013. JPMorgan paid $290 million to victims and $75 million to settle the Virgin Islands suit and denies helping Epstein commit crimes.

Texas flips as Talarico and Hinojosa win statewide

tags: politics, elections
sources: @groundnews, @aaronparnas

Democrat James Talarico defeated Republican Ken Paxton to become the first Democrat elected to Texas's US Senate delegation since 1988, winning by about 12 points after a campaign dominated by living costs and more than $500 million in spending, including $158 million from Elon Musk backing Paxton. Gina Hinojosa defeated Greg Abbott to become the state's first Latina governor. Democrats also flipped the Texas state House and the State Board of Education. Trump privately regrets endorsing Paxton rather than John Cornyn, according to reporting.

Musk faces investigations and a Texas land sale freeze after election losses

tags: politics, tech
sources: @oafnation_actual, @aaronparnas

Musk spent about $445 million on federal races with little return: three of the 43 House Republicans he backed won, and six of his seven Senate picks lost. Texas governor-elect Gina Hinojosa has requested a pause on state land sales to his companies, including the sale of Boca Chica State Park to SpaceX, saying any relationship must be on the state's terms. Senate Democrats are preparing an investigation into restrictions on Ukraine's military satellite communications and have told Musk to preserve documents after SpaceX's Starshield service was slowed in October, degrading Ukrainian air defences. Musk says the US government controls Starshield limits.

Trump orders ICE operations scaled back after deportations reached people Melania Trump knew

tags: immigration, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

Trump told Stephen Miller to roll back immigration enforcement operations after Melania Trump said she knew people who were being deported, according to reporting confirmed by the Wall Street Journal. The intervention came after the mass deportation campaign affected people connected to the Trump family. Immigration enforcement was cited by 73% of voters as a crucial or major factor in their midterm vote.

Russell Brand convicted of rape and sexual assault

tags: legal
sources: @groundnews, @aaronparnas

A jury at Southwark Crown Court in London convicted Russell Brand of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault, clearing him of two further rape charges and one count of attempted indecent assault. The judge warned the 51-year-old to expect a custodial sentence, with sentencing to come later. Brand had denied every allegation, arguing the encounters were consensual or that accusers had invented or recast events.

Voters decide major ballot measures on taxes, elections and criminal sentencing

tags: politics, elections
sources: @groundnews

Montana approved I-194 barring corporate, union and some nonprofit election spending, an approach designed to test the Citizens United ruling. Voters approved photo ID requirements in Nevada, Ohio and North Carolina while rejecting California's Prop 39 ID measure, and California's Prop 40 billionaire wealth tax trailed 56% to 44% in an uncalled race. Florida approved a fivefold increase in the homestead exemption that could cost local governments about $5 billion in the first year, Colorado approved mandatory life without parole for child sex trafficking, Massachusetts rejected repealing recreational marijuana sales, and Idaho voters rejected restoring abortion rights up to viability. Alaska's measure to end ranked choice voting remained uncalled with 'No' leading 52% to 48%.

Washington and Colorado voters approve transgender school sports restrictions

tags: politics, legal
sources: @groundnews

Ballot initiatives restricting transgender students' participation in school athletics passed in Washington with more than 56% support and in Colorado with 52%. Washington will exclude biologically male students from girls' teams and require medical providers to certify eligibility; Colorado will classify teams by sex or as coed with participation tied to birth sex. Supporters went to voters after Democratic governors and legislators in both states declined to pass bans. More than half of US states now have some form of restriction on transgender athletes.

Israel certifies election with Netanyahu's bloc short of a majority

tags: politics, elections
sources: @groundnews

Israel's Central Elections Committee certified the Oct. 27 results 15-14 after an audit of 9,069 polling stations found no evidence of irregularities. Netanyahu's bloc won 53 of 120 Knesset seats, eight short of a majority, Gadi Eisenkot's opposition bloc won 48 and Arab parties won a record 19. Likud had sought to delay certification over fraud allegations against Arab parties, and the attorney general rejected a Shin Bet request to question Arab lawmakers without evidence. President Isaac Herzog has 28 days, with a possible extension, to pick a leader to form a government, and both main blocs have ruled out coalitions with the Arab parties.

Russia agreed to supply Iran with 90 missile launchers, documents show

tags: defence, war
sources: @oafnation_actual

Industry documents reviewed by the Financial Times list 90 APU-L helicopter missile launchers for a buyer coded K-10, identified as Iran. The launchers carry LMUR missiles that Russia has used widely in Ukraine. The documents do not show whether the launchers were delivered.

Finland accuses US of withholding paid-for Patriot interceptors from Ukraine

tags: war, defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

Finnish Defence Minister Antti Häkkänen said Europe has already paid for Patriot interceptors but Washington has not approved their delivery, accusing the US of playing politics. President Zelenskyy said Ukraine has waited nearly a month for Pete Hegseth to sign off. Russia is preparing large winter attacks on Ukrainian energy sites.

Poland arrests suspects accused of spying and supplying weapons parts to Russia

tags: legal, defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

Poland's Internal Security Agency said it arrested a group accused of illegally sending Russia significant quantities of components used to produce ammunition and weapons systems. The suspects include five Polish nationals and a 37-year-old Russian woman. The agency described the activity as espionage on behalf of Russia.

Newsom commutes all 548 California death sentences

tags: legal, politics
sources: @groundnews

California Gov. Gavin Newsom announced he plans to commute the death sentences of all 548 inmates on the state's death row to life imprisonment without parole, arguing that capital punishment undermines justice and disproportionately affects people of color. About 60% of the commutations require California Supreme Court approval before his term ends in January. California has not executed a prisoner since 2006 and Newsom imposed a moratorium in 2019. The death penalty remains legal in the state, so courts can still impose new death sentences.

Paraguay's president resigns after digital bank collapse

tags: politics, markets
sources: @groundnews, @ericmoutsos

President Santiago Peña resigned following the collapse of Ueno Bank, a digital lender serving more than 60% of the country's adults and holding roughly $800 million in public deposits before regulators seized it over financial irregularities. His resignation followed impeachment threats from his own Colorado Party, protests involving clashes with riot police and the detention of eight bank executives. Peña held a stake in Ueno's holding company until last year and had appointed a former Ueno executive to lead the central bank. Accounts were frozen, leaving millions of customers without access to savings and pensions.

Hegseth expands National Guard role in Washington DC

tags: politics, policing
sources: @oafnation_actual

A memo obtained by Politico shows Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth authorized National Guard troops in Washington to use boats, marked police cars, Humvees and tactical vehicles. Guard boats will support police operations in Anacostia. The deployment began in August 2025 under Trump's crime emergency declaration.

Democratic leadership fights open over Jeffries and Schumer

tags: politics
sources: @oafnation_actual, @total.hypocrisy

Sen. Chris Van Hollen said he will not challenge Chuck Schumer for Senate Democratic leader, telling Fox 5 DC he is not looking for the job and is considering a 2028 presidential run; Sen.-elect Abdul El-Sayed said Van Hollen would be an excellent majority leader. Separately, pressure is building against Hakeem Jeffries becoming House speaker over his ties to pro-Israel donors. Critics argue the same scrutiny applied to Jeffries should extend to Schumer, citing his April 2026 vote against blocking $450 million in arms transfers to Israel.

Investigation alleges undisclosed political funding of creator network

tags: politics, media
sources: @total.hypocrisy

An investigation into Chorus, a network of nearly 200 political content creators co-founded by Brian Tyler Cohen and Stuart Perlmutter, says creators are paid without being required to disclose it and that the money is now untraceable. Funding previously flowed through the 1630 Fund and Arabella Advisors, but from January 2026 Chorus routed donations through its own nonprofit, the Creator Collective, during a House Oversight Committee inquiry. The committee sent document requests in November 2025 and March 2026 and issued a subpoena to the 1630 Fund in May 2026; only 135 and 62 pages respectively have been produced, with members calling the redactions obstructive. A related for-profit agency, Good Influence, received $10,000 from the Haley Stevens campaign, which had taken roughly $30 million in AIPAC support.

Democratic socialist Nithya Raman projected to unseat Karen Bass in Los Angeles

tags: politics, elections
sources: @groundnews

Decision Desk HQ projects city council member Nithya Raman defeating Mayor Karen Bass 51.1% to 48.33%. If the result holds, Raman would be the first Asian American to lead the second-largest city in the United States. She was born in Kerala, India, moved to the US at six and naturalized at 22, and campaigned on homelessness, rent and housing costs, tenant protections and public safety.

Chinese court takes up COVID defamation case against Missouri

tags: legal, health
sources: @groundnews

A court in Wuhan has accepted a defamation lawsuit against the state of Missouri and three people who have led its attorney general's office, Eric Schmitt, Andrew Bailey and Catherine Hanaway. The Wuhan city government, the Wuhan Institute of Virology and the Chinese Academy of Sciences allege the defendants spread falsehoods about the pandemic and are seeking an apology, reputational remedies and damages reported at 356.44 billion yuan. The case follows Missouri's April 2020 suit seeking compensation from Hubei and other Chinese defendants for pandemic-related economic harm.

Drug patent tactics blamed for high US prescription costs

tags: health, politics
sources: @hunteralexanderhowell

Brand-name drug manufacturers are accused of using patent thickets, product hopping and pay-for-delay agreements to keep generic competitors off the market and prices high. Pay-for-delay involves paying potential generic rivals to stay out of the market, while continuation patents extend exclusivity through minor modifications. Supporters of the EPIC Act say it has bipartisan backing in Congress and would curb these practices.

Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern merger weighed on infrastructure grounds

tags: markets
sources: @hunteralexanderhowell

A proposed merger between Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern would create a coast-to-coast rail network. The chief executive of Schneider has argued it would bring greater connectivity, faster speeds and more reliable infrastructure, citing cross-border operations with Mexico as a precedent. Analysts have said the combination would reduce transit times and open new markets and jobs.

Utah ballot count continues with legislative power measure defeated

tags: politics, elections
sources: @carolinegleich

Early Utah results show Senate Majority Leader Kirk Cullimore, who was running to replace Stuart Adams as Senate president, likely out, and Amendment B, which would have given the legislature more power, defeated. Several races remain too close to call and the count could take up to a couple of weeks. Voters whose ballots were set aside can track them at trackmyballot.utah.gov, must respond to county clerk notices, and provisional voters needing to show ID face a deadline of close of business Monday, November 9.

Nineteen-year-old elected clerk of nation's fourth-largest county

tags: politics, legal
sources: @groundnews

Arizona State University student Sebastian Matta, 19, won election as Maricopa County Superior Court clerk, overseeing court records for the fourth most populous county in the country. Republican opponent Jeff Dial, a former state senator, conceded by phone. Matta said he plans to spend his first months building relationships with staff and assuring them their positions are secure, delaying campaign proposals by several months or a year.

Foreign leaders cast US midterm result as a shift in global alignment

tags: politics
sources: @aaronparnas, @groundnews

Leaders across Europe, the Middle East and the Americas responded to the Democratic sweep. Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez said Americans voted against policies that impoverish people, against hate and against climate denial; Iran's parliament speaker said Americans said no to war; and the UK leader framed the result as an opportunity to unite around cost of living. Israeli opposition leader Yair Golan said the results show how toxic Netanyahu has become in both US parties and warned of sanctions and isolation. Barack Obama called it a message in favour of politics that brings people together, while Russia characterised Trump's position as negative.

Iowa Democrat who ended campaign wins House seat anyway

tags: politics, elections
sources: @groundnews

Democrat Eric Armstrong won an Iowa House seat despite withdrawing from the race in September because of health problems, beating Republican Keith Jones by roughly 865 votes, a nine-point margin. The retired railroad executive succeeds Democrat Josh Turek, who won a US Senate seat. Armstrong said he will do his best to represent constituents but is still struggling with health issues.
